text: Because a scientific hypothesis confronts the 'tribunal of experience' only bundled together with auxiliary assumptions, a failed prediction never conclusively refutes any single hypothesis on its own; this holist point about testing is known as the ___ thesis.
explanation: The Duhem-Quine thesis holds that hypotheses face experience only in conjunction with auxiliaries, so the 'blame' for an anomaly can always be relocated (as when a Uranus anomaly yielded Neptune but a similar Mercury anomaly yielded the never-found Vulcan). This underwrites underdetermination and blocks the Popperian idea that a single observation cleanly falsifies a lone hypothesis.
